newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: La Tondena sets 2.7 bln-peso expansion.
newsitem.headline: La Tondena sets 2.7 bln-peso expansion.

text.p: La Tondena Distillers Inc (LTDI) has set an expansion programme of 2.5 billion to 2.7 billion pesos this year, Joseph John Ong, the firm's vice president told analysts after a stockholders meeting on Thursday.
LTDI is the liquor unit of food and beverage firm San Miguel Corp.
He said about 800 to 900 million pesos will be spent to double the capacity of its distillery in the central Philippines to 90 million litres by the end of the third quarter from 45 million litres.

The rest will be spent in expanding the capacity of its carbon dioxide plant, starting construction of the second distillery south of Manila which may be operational by the end of 1998; and putting up a third mineral water bottling plant which may start by the second half of next year, Ong said.
As a result of the expansion programme, the firm had instituted a seven percent increase in its liquor prices in March to offset the higher operating expenses, Ong said.
The March increase followed a 10 percent hike in December to cover for the higher excise taxes slapped on liquor.
The expansion programme is expected to be funded by one billion pesos worth of long-term debt and the rest through internally-generated cash, Ong said.

La Tondena officials told stockholders the firm's liquor sales volume is expected to grow faster than the industry average of five to six percent but not at the same pace as its historical growth of 15 to 16 percent.
Sales are expected to be buoyed by the start of election spending for the May 1998 national elections, officials said.
"Normally we do expect higher consumption during election years relative to normal years. Remember the election campaign period unofficially starts now," Ong said.
Liquor contributes to 80 percent of the firm's revenues, while bottled water and juices comprise the rest.
Currently, La Tondena enjoys leadership in the hard liquor segment with a 59 percent market share. It has a 24 percent share in the bottled water market and less than 20 percent in juices.
